candidates.changed_node: root rebuilt as quality minus a new TS_CORR(63) whose volume argument is the grafted ($open + 1e-8) turnover normaliser
candidates.rationale: Donates ($open + 1e-8) from A and ($high - $low) from B, exactly 3 nodes each. A's price anchor is reused as a normaliser for volume rather than for book value: $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8) recovers split-robust share turnover on the raw price scale (raw dollar volume over raw open, no adjusted-close mixing). Correlating that with the daily range over a quarter is a price-impact state, and the child uses it as a discount on A's profitability leg. Fusion: quality priced net of how much of a name's range is bought by trading activity. A ranks quality unconditionally; B ranks the range/volume link with no cross-section of quality.

candidates.changed_node: B's margin-delta leg re-wrapped in CS_ZSCORE and multiplied by a new illiquidity rank built on A's grafted ($high - $low)
candidates.rationale: Donates ($high - $low) from A and TS_DELTA($operating_margin, 63) from B. A's raw materials are recombined from a correlation into a level: range volatility per dollar traded, an Amihud-style price-impact scaler. That scaler is the conditioning variable on B's margin trend, since fundamental news diffuses slowly where trading is expensive, so the same margin delta should carry more weight in illiquid names and less in liquid ones. Signed z-score times a [0,1] rank keeps the fundamental's sign and scales only its magnitude. Neither parent conditions: B is an unconditional fundamental composite, A an unconditional liquidity statistic.

candidates.changed_node: A's two additive legs replaced by their product inside CS_ZSCORE, signed by B's grafted CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe))
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_DELTA($operating_margin, 63) from A and CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) from B. A adds margin trend and turnover level as two separate ranks; the child multiplies them, which is the DuPont identity (ROA = margin x turnover), so Dmargin x turnover is the ROA improvement that margin expansion actually delivers. B's demeaned quality rank then signs it: improvement in an already profitable firm persists, the same improvement in an unprofitable one is noise. Interaction neither parent has: A has no quality conditioner, B has no trend term.

candidates.changed_node: A's volatility scaler re-pointed from the quality leg to B's leverage-change term; range normalised by TS_MEAN($open, 42) instead of A's 10-day open
candidates.rationale: Donates CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) and ($high - $low) from A, TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from B. A's mechanism is that a fundamental signal should be scaled by relative range, realised volatility on the raw open scale; B's is that leverage growth is bad. The child moves A's volatility scaler off the quality leg and onto B's leverage-growth penalty: debt expansion is a distress signal specifically in high-volatility names and close to noise in quiet ones. B penalises Dleverage unconditionally, A has no balance-sheet term.

candidates.changed_node: A's price ratio rebuilt as TS_MAX($high, 21) over the grafted ($open + 1e-8) and made the multiplier on B's Dleverage
candidates.rationale: Donates ($open + 1e-8) from A and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from B. A's two fundamental legs collapse into one cash-based profitability measure ($roa net of the accrual gap) instead of two separately ranked legs, and A's price anchor becomes a drawdown state: TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8) exceeds 1 when the open sits far below the month's high, raw scale on both sides. That state multiplies B's leverage change, so balance-sheet expansion is punished where the price has already fallen (distress) and is near neutral for names at their highs (growth financing). Conditioning variable neither parent has.

candidates.changed_node: root replaced by an IF_ELSE regime switch on TS_RANK of B's grafted TS_MEAN($high, 21), branching to quality or to A's negated Dleverage
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from A and TS_MEAN($high, 21) from B. B's price term is recast as a self-referential trend state, where the 21-day average high sits inside its own 126-day range, so there is no cross-sectional price-level comparison and no division. That state is used as a regime switch rather than a multiplier: in names holding in the upper half of their own range, rank on profitability, since quality is rewarded when the market is engaged; in drawdown names, rank on deleveraging, which is what matters when the price is falling. Both branches are [0,1] ranks so the switch does not distort scale. A adds its terms, B multiplies, neither selects between factors.

candidates.changed_node: B's margin delta re-normalised by TS_RANK over its own 126-day history and differenced against a price-extension rank built on A's grafted TS_MAX($high, 21)
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_MAX($high, 21) from A and TS_DELTA($operating_margin, 63) from B. The fundamental leg is normalised against the firm's own history (is this margin change large for this firm?) while the price leg is normalised cross-sectionally, and the child is the divergence between the two: a monthly peak standing well above the two-month average high says the move has already happened. Long firms whose own margin trend is at a local extreme and whose price has not extended, short the reverse. A has no trend term, B no price term, and neither mixes a time-series with a cross-sectional normaliser.

candidates.changed_node: A's grafted TS_MEAN($open, 10) turned from a divisor into a breakout reference, and the resulting rank made the confirmation weight on B's margin delta
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_MEAN($open, 10) from A and TS_DELTA($operating_margin, 63) from B. A's 10-day open average is reused as a breakout reference instead of a price normaliser: today's high measured against it in units of the open's own 10-day dispersion, raw scale throughout and a short enough span that unadjusted-price splits are a minor risk. That breakout rank is the confirmation weight on B's margin trend, demeaned so its sign is cross-sectional: improving margins count most where the price is confirming, deteriorating margins hurt most where the price is extended. Fusion is fundamental momentum gated by price confirmation; A scales a static quality rank by range, B is unconditioned.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
